content: Durable execution engines (Temporal, Inngest, Restate) persist workflow state so a crashed process resumes exactly where it left off; Temporal replays full event history, Inngest treats human-in-the-loop as a native primitive while Temporal composes it from Signals+Selectors. Trade-off: determinism constraints and versioning pain for long-running workflows whose code changes mid-flight. For a single-node self-hosted daemon, borrowing the concepts (durable event log, checkpointed step boundaries, signal-driven resume) without adopting the engine avoids a heavy operational dependency.
